paper.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial multi-armed bandit with semi-bandit feedback and smooth index-invariant reward (lower bound)
unmapped: Known general (possibly non-monotone) differentiable reward function r(S; mu) of the means of the selected base arms, assumed smooth index invariant
Base-arm observations in [0,1], possibly correlated across arms
Hard instances are I-disjoint action sets (a common subset I in all actions, other arms in exactly one action)
settings.definition_quote: Denote the number of arms (`base arms') by $m$, and let $\mathcal{S}\subset 2^{[m]}$ be the set of possible actions ... The number of base arms in each action is bounded by $|S|\le K$ ... the arms generate an observation vector $X^{(t)}\in[0,1]^m$ ... The goal of the agent is to maximize a known reward function $r(S;\mu)$

symbols.Delta_i: gap of suboptimal action (super arm) S
symbols.KL_i: KL divergence between the joint observation distributions of action S and of the optimal action

conditions: reward function smooth index invariant, |S| = K for all actions
there is an arm i not in I in S* with non-deterministic observation and nonzero gradient of reward

symbols.K_I: K - |I|, effective action size for common set I
symbols.gamma_tilde_sq: modified Gini-weighted smoothness tilde gamma_g^2(mu; I), maximized jointly with K_I over I

conditions: exists an I-disjoint instance with minimal gap Delta and optimal-action means mu (any mu in [0,1]^K)

source.label: theorem:dependent_lower_bound
source.quote: For any $\mu\in[0,1]^K$ and any small enough $\Delta>0$, there exists an instance of an $I$-disjoint bandit problem with minimal gap $\Delta$ and $\E[\nu_{S^*}]=\mu$, such that the expected regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded by $\liminf_{T\to\infty} \frac{\E[R(t)]}{\ln T} \ge \max_I \frac{(m-2K)\tilde{\gamma}_g^2(\mu;I)}{8K_I\Delta} \triangleq DB^*_r(\Delta;\mu)$.

results.notes: Max over I omitted from expression; gamma_tilde_sq/K_I denote the maximizing pair. Paper notes this reproduces linear (Omega(mK log T/Delta)) and PMC bounds.

symbols.M_items: number of summands M in the sum reward tilde r = sum_i r(mu_i)
symbols.m_base: number of base arms per summand (paper's m)
symbols.gamma_tilde_sq: modified Gini-weighted smoothness, maximized over I

conditions: reward is a sum of M copies of a smooth index invariant reward function

source.label: corollary: sum index invariant dependent
source.quote: Then, for any $\mu\in[0,1]^K$, there exists a CMAB instance that aims to maximize $\tilde{r}$ and has a minimal gap $\Delta$, such that the optimal action has means $\mu_i=\mu$ for all $i\in[M]$ and the expected regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded by $\liminf_{T\to\infty} \frac{\E[R(t)]}{\ln T} \ge M^2\cdot DB^*_r(\Delta;\mu)$.

results.notes: Sum-reward extension used to recover PMC lower bounds.

symbols.KL_nu: KL divergence between the suboptimal and optimal action distributions nu, nu*

conditions: instance constructed for the given strategy and horizon

source.label: lemma:generalIndependentBound
source.quote:
Then, for any horizon $T$ and any strategy $\psi$, there exists an $I$-disjoint CMAB problem with arm distribution $\unu'$ such that $
u_{S^*}=\mu^*$ and its regret under strategy $\psi$ is bounded by $\E_{\unu'}[R(T)] \ge T\Delta(1- rac{K_I}{m-K} -\sqrt{ rac{1}{2} rac{TK_I}{m-K}\kl(
u,
u^*)})$.

results.notes: General technical lower bound; Delta is the gap between nu* and nu (all suboptimal actions share the gap).

symbols.gamma_tilde: modified Gini-weighted smoothness tilde gamma_g(mu; I), maximized over I

conditions: any mu in [0,1]^K: instance has E[nu'_{S*}] = mu

source.label: theorem:independent_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $r$ be a smooth index invariant reward function and assume that $m\ge3K$. Then, for any $\mu\in[0,1]^K$, any $T\ge T_0$ and for any strategy $\psi$, there exists an $I$-disjoint CMAB problem $\unu'$ with $\E[\nu'_{S^*}]=\mu$ such that its regret under strategy $\psi$ is bounded by $\E_{\unu'}[R(T)] \ge \max_{I}\frac{\tilde{\gamma}_g(\mu;I)}{32}\sqrt{\frac{T(m-K)}{K_I}} \triangleq IB^*_r(\mu)$.

results.notes: Theorem number not printed (restatable environment). Combined with Proposition (smoothness relation), paper states Omega-tilde(gamma_g sqrt(m T)) for monotone rewards informally.

symbols.M_items: number of summands M in sum reward
symbols.m_base: number of base arms per summand
symbols.gamma_tilde: modified Gini-weighted smoothness, maximized over I

conditions: reward is a sum of M copies of a smooth index invariant reward

source.label: corollary: sum index invariant independent
source.quote: Under the notations of Corollary 7, if $m\ge3K$, then for any $\mu\in[0,1]^K$, any $T\ge T_0$ and for any strategy $\psi$, there exists CMAB problem $\unu'$ such that the optimal action has means $\mu_i=\mu$ for all $i\in[M]$ whose regret under strategy $\psi$ is bounded by $\E_{\unu'}[R(T)] \ge M\cdot IB^*_r(\mu)$.
